evals.prompt: All leaves of our roadmap campaign `oauth-support` are merged into the integration branch `feat/oauth-support`. The campaign adds an OAuth login provider abstraction, a GitHub provider and a token-refresh fix in the `auth` package. Land it on main. Write the PR title and body you would use, and list the steps to get it merged.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as the Reviewed PR lane (a campaign landing), writes a `merge(auth): ...` title that will become the merge subject, a body that becomes the merge body (why, what lands, verification), and landing steps: rebase onto main, force-with-lease, wait for CI, maintainer approval, merge with a merge commit (not squash), then pull main.

assertions.name: reviewed-lane
assertions.description: Identifies the change as needing maintainer review because it lands a campaign

assertions.name: merge-subject-title
assertions.description: The PR title follows the merge-commit subject shape

assertions.name: rebase-before-merge
assertions.description: Rebases onto main before merging

assertions.name: merge-commit-not-squash
assertions.description: Merges with a merge commit, never a squash

assertions.name: no-squash-instruction
assertions.description: Does not instruct a squash merge

assertions.name: no-fork-dev-model
assertions.description: Does not fall back to a fork / dev-branch model

evals.prompt: I have a single Python package managed with uv (pyproject.toml, src/ layout), conventional commits already in use, no release automation yet, and I want versions, a changelog, tags and GitHub Releases cut automatically when work lands on main. PyPI publishing can wait. What release setup should I adopt?
evals.expected_output: Derives the tooling from the repo's contents: prefers Python-native tooling (e.g. python-semantic-release or commitizen) so CI needs no Node toolchain, covers the capability checklist (version from commits, changelog, tag, GitHub Release, publishing deferred), and wires a release job in CI gated on the tests, triggered by pushes to main, with a [skip ci] bump commit.

assertions.name: python-native-tool
assertions.description: Recommends a Python-native release tool

assertions.name: ci-on-main
assertions.description: Releases from CI after landing on main, not locally

assertions.name: gated-release-job
assertions.description: The release job depends on the gates

assertions.name: skip-ci-bump
assertions.description: Mentions the bot bump commit skipping CI

assertions.name: no-release-pr
assertions.description: Does not set up a release PR ceremony

evals.prompt: I merged a PR into main an hour ago, CI was green, but no new version, tag or GitHub Release appeared. The PR had two commits: `docs(readme): clarify install steps` and `chore(deps): bump pytest`. What went wrong and what should I do?
evals.expected_output: Explains that neither commit is a release-type commit (docs and chore release nothing under the repo's convention), so the release job correctly found nothing to release; says how to confirm (commits since the last tag, the release job log saying nothing to release) and that a release happens when a release-type commit (e.g. fix/feat) lands; does not suggest tagging by hand or running a release locally.

assertions.name: no-release-type-commit
assertions.description: Identifies that the commits are not release-type

assertions.name: confirm-since-last-tag
assertions.description: Says how to confirm against the last tag or the job log

assertions.name: no-manual-release
assertions.description: Does not recommend a manual tag or a local release

evals.prompt: Our library has a handful of internal users. I'd like to add a `dev` branch that publishes `-dev.N` prereleases, so features can bake there before they reach main. Set that up.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: recommends staying on a single channel (main) because a long-lived dev branch doubles integration, drifts and accumulates an unreleased backlog; names the adoption triggers that would justify a channel (many external users, regressions reaching users, downstream pinning) and, if a channel is ever needed, the lagged release-candidate pattern from main rather than a separate dev branch. Unfinished work belongs on topic branches.

assertions.name: single-channel
assertions.description: Recommends keeping one channel

assertions.name: adoption-triggers
assertions.description: Names when a channel would be justified

assertions.name: rc-pattern
assertions.description: Points to the lagged release-candidate pattern as the escalation

assertions.name: cost-of-dev-branch
assertions.description: States the cost of a long-lived development branch

evals.prompt: I just wrote a findings report under __reports__/perf/ and updated two roadmap node statuses. Nothing under src/ changed. Should this go through a pull request before it lands on main?
evals.expected_output: Chooses the Direct lane: the change releases nothing and touches neither CI nor release machinery, so it lands with local branch-to-parent integration (if branched) then pull and push to main, with no PR and no maintainer approval; notes a wrong lane is cheap because CI still checks pushes to main.

assertions.name: direct-lane
assertions.description: Chooses the direct lane

assertions.name: reason-releases-nothing
assertions.description: Justifies it by the change releasing nothing

assertions.name: no-pr-required
assertions.description: Does not demand a reviewed PR
